title: Cross-service reliability coupling strategy and SLO runway
content:
Purpose
-----
This is a working plan for reducing fragile coupling between feature services and the inference runtime, and for establishing a 90-day SLO runway that surface-stakes, decision points, and handoffs across eng-site-reliability, platform-engineering, product-hosted-api and customer-success.

Context (short)
----------------
We continue to see higher-than-expected blast radius when model-serving capacity or KV cache TTLs change. Multiple teams own parts of the surface that contribute to customer-visible latency and error budgets. The goal here is to:
- map coupling points (where a change in A causes an SLO impact in B)
- define a minimal experiment to reduce two high-risk coupling paths in Q1
- create a reusable SLO runway (measurement, alerting, rollout gates) for future features

Scope and non-goals
--------------------
In-scope: cross-service request flows that touch the hosted API, dedicated pools, and platform routing layer. Include telemetry, feature flags, rollout gating, and emergency fallback policies.
Out-of-scope: lower-priority internal infra (CI pipelines, infra provisioning) unless it directly affects runtime latency. Not a model-quality initiative (handled by applied-ml).

High-level objectives (SMART)
----------------------------
- Reduce incidents caused by routing/config mismatch by 60% on the two highest-coupled services within 90 days of pilot start.
- Ship an SLO runway template and two pre-populated dashboards that teams can adopt in <30 days.
- Define and validate rollback/fallback policy for routing-tier failures with <3% false-positive rollbacks during canaries.

Stakeholders and roles
-----------------------
- Initiative lead: Aisha Patel (platform-engineering) — overall plan and cross-team coordination
- SLO design / telemetry: Michael Chen (eng-site-reliability) — SLI definitions, dashboards, alert tuning
- Runtime / serving: Sofia Rivera (serving-runtime) — changes to routing, KV cache, batching defaults for experiments
- Product owner & rollout: Priya Desai (product-hosted-api) — gating and UX impact reviews
- Customer ops: Liam O'Connor — customer communications and post-incident follow-through

Primary deliverables
---------------------
1) Coupling map: a lightweight graph (CSV) listing service A -> service B coupling type, owner, SLI impacted, current error budget burn rate.
2) SLO runway template: SLO text + SLI implementation pointers + alert thresholds + canary gating checklist + rollback decision matrix.
3) Two pilot mitigations shipped to canary: (a) routing fallback path with graceful degradation; (b) KV-cache prefix-anchoring + shorter default TTL for noisy tenants.
4) Post-pilot runbook and handoff package for platform teams to adopt.

Milestones and timeline (90-day runway)
---------------------------------------
Week 0 (planning): kickoff, coupling discovery workshop, finalize pilot targets (2 coupling paths) — owner: Aisha
Week 1–2: collect telemetry, draft coupling map, SLI candidate list — owner: Michael
Week 3: SLO runway template completed (draft) and review with product & SRE — owner: Michael + Priya
Week 4–6: Implement pilot mitigation A (routing fallback) in staging and start 1% canary — owner: Sofia
Week 5–8: Implement pilot mitigation B (KV TTL + prefixing) in staging and start 1% canary — owner: Sofia
Week 7–10: iterate on alerts, tune thresholds, escalate false positives/negatives to decision log — owner: Michael
Week 10–12: expand canary to 25% if metrics ok, finalize runbook, and begin handoff to platform-runway team — owner: Aisha
Week 12+: retro, write final recommendations, schedule adoption sessions with feature teams — owner: Aisha + Priya

Measurement and success criteria
--------------------------------
Primary metrics (SLIs we will track):
- P50/P95 server-side latency for cross-service calls that touch routing layer
- Per-tenant error budget burn rate (5m window and 1h trend)
- Canary rollback frequency and root cause classification
- Customer-facing incidents attributable to coupling (postmortem tags)
Success threshold example: pilot path reduces error budget burn rate by >=60% for the impacted SLO over the 30-day post-rollout window.

Decision framework and gates
---------------------------
- Canary gate: proceed from 1% -> 25% only if: no increase in 5-minute error rate >1.5x baseline, P95 latency delta < 25%, and alert noise under 2 actionable alerts per week.
- Rollback decision: automatic rollback trigger on sustained 5-minute error rate > 3x baseline OR P95 latency increase > 100ms + customer complaints > threshold. Manual rollback allowed with approver list (SRE oncall, runtime lead, product owner).
- Decommission gate: when fallback reduces customer impact and coupling paths removed in code/config, document and close coupling map entry.

Communication and run cadence
-----------------------------
- Weekly 30m sync (Wednesdays) with initiative stakeholders — quick status, top risks, action owners.
- Bi-weekly demo where runtime team shows canary telemetry and any mitigations.
- Channel: #reliability-coupling (Slack) for async updates, decision log pinned.
- Stakeholder report: one-pager after major milestone (canary start, canary expansion, final retro) sent to execs and program board.

Risk register (top entries)
--------------------------
1) False positive rollbacks: can cause unnecessary user impact. Mitigation: improved synthetic checks + staggered canaries.
2) Observability gaps: missing distributed trace tags across hops. Mitigation: small tracing shim and incremental instrumentation tickets.
3) Cross-team alignment slips: features land without gating. Mitigation: add SLO runway adoption as release checklist item in product-ops.
4) Customer baseline variance: noisy tenants mask effect. Mitigation: tenant bucketing and controlled experiments.

Runbook handoff checklist (minimum)
----------------------------------
- Coupling map CSV uploaded to Confluence + canonical path to raw traces
- SLO runway template copied and SLI instrumentation links verified
- Playbook: how to start a canary, who to call, rollback steps, postmortem template
- Dashboard links and burn-rate alert rules exported as JSON and stored in ops-config repo
- Schedule 1-hour adoption workshop with platform-runway team and two feature teams

Open questions / TODOs
----------------------
- Q: Do we need to expand to dedicated customers earlier? Answer pending from sales/CS (Priya to follow up).
- TODO: Michael to enumerate 6 telemetry gaps and open instrumentation tickets (target Wk2).
- TODO: Sofia to prototype a minimal fallback in staging and post an implementation doc (GH PR by Wk4).
- TODO: Aisha to confirm 2 pilot coupling paths by end of kickoff week.

Raw action items (first 14 days)
--------------------------------
- A1: Schedule coupling discovery workshop (Aisha) — invite SRE, runtime, product, CS — 2024-10-18
- A2: Export current burn-rate per service and baseline P95 for routing layer (Michael) — due 2024-10-22
- A3: Prototype routing fallback toggle and doc initial plan (Sofia) — due 2024-11-01
- A4: Add SLO runway adoption item to product release checklist (Priya) — due 2024-10-25

Notes to self / working thoughts
-------------------------------
- Keep the coupling map intentionally simple: owner, impact SLI, brief description, evidence link. Avoid deep graph complexity on first pass.
- Focus the pilot on one noisy tenant and one cross-service path to keep scope tight.
- Plan for a short tabletop exercise mid-canaary to validate human ops responses.

Appendix: minimal SLO text example (starter)
-------------------------------------------
SLO: Hosted API end-to-end successful responses (non-stream)
Target: 99.5% over 30d (customer-impacting errors only)
SLI: ratio of successful 200-range responses to total production requests, excluding planned maintenance windows and non-retryable client errors.
Alerting: warn at 99.7% (burn rate 1.2), page at 99.3% (burn rate 3.0)
Owner: product-hosted-api + eng-site-reliability (joint)

If you're reading this and want to be involved, ping me (Aisha) in #reliability-coupling or drop a quick note on the Confluence page linked above.

---
Draft version: expect edits. This doc is intentionally conversational and lightweight; will convert to a canonical playbook after pilot complete.
